purpose: The citable, field-pinnable identity of AFP's current wire and interface surface. `interface_set_id` digests the identifier-granular interface surface: message classes, telemetry predicates, typed wire records, presentation profiles, published profiles, message subject subtrees, predicate status and public-input structure names, the session envelope identifier, the NATS subject root, and the composed ZKA, ZKC, and AFP-KDC versions. Prose fields are excluded from the digest preimage by construction, so editorial changes do not change the interface surface. `document_revision` identifies the current published specification document and is checked against its front matter; it is deliberately not referenced by the protocol-family manifest. See `digest_scope` for the field-content boundary and its separate gates.

digest_scope.covers: The presence, identity and declared status of each interface element: message class ids and their section 12.4 subject subtrees; telemetry predicate ids, frozen/current status, and the NAME of each predicate's public-input structure; typed wire record ids; presentation profile ids; published profile names and their reference/experimental status; the session envelope identifier; the NATS subject root; and the ZKA/ZKC/AFP-KDC versions this specification composes with. This is exactly the scope of version_discipline.interface_change.
digest_scope.does_not_cover: The FIELD CONTENT or canonical value mapping of the typed records themselves. Adding, renaming, reordering or retyping a field inside `interface AfpEnvelope { ... }` or `interface AfpInstanceAttestationPublicInputsV2 { ... }`, or changing how an AFP value is projected into a composed protocol's fixed-width field, leaves interface_set_id byte-identical because wire_records is projected to [id] and telemetry_predicates carries only the public-input structure's name. Do not read a green interface_set_id as evidence that no record field or cross-protocol value mapping changed.

digest_scope.why_not_digested: Extending interface_set_id to cover the record bodies was considered and rejected for this phase. Those bodies are TypeScript blocks carrying inline `//` comments, so digesting them would pull prose back into the preimage -- the exact coupling this file exists to remove, one layer down and harder to see, because it would present as a cryptographic surface change. Byte-identical test pins catch a field addition without that hazard; they fail loudly and are re-blessed deliberately, in a test diff a reviewer reads.

interface_set_id_derivation: sha256 over b"afp:interface-surface:v1" || canonical-JSON(preimage), where canonical JSON is UTF-8 with object keys sorted and no insignificant whitespace (RFC 8785 subset). The projection is IDENTIFIER-granular -- see `digest_scope` -- and preimage is exactly {"composes_with": {...}, "envelope": "...", "message_classes": [...], "nats_subject_root": "...", "presentation_profiles": [...], "profiles": [...], "telemetry_predicates": [...], "wire_records": [...]} built by PROJECTING each member to a fixed field list, with absent fields serialized as null: message_classes -> [id, subject_subtree]; telemetry_predicates -> [id, status, public_inputs_interface]; wire_records -> [id]; profiles -> [name, status]; composes_with -> [zka, zkc, kdc]. Array order is preserved as published. Every other field of this file is outside the preimage, including `interface_version`, `document_revision`, `family_epoch`, and prose fields such as purpose, note, notes, description, rationale, summary, reason, and spec_reference. The exclusion is by construction: the preimage whitelists sections, each member is projected to a whitelisted field tuple, scripts/check_afp_interface_surface.py refuses to digest prose-shaped field names, and it fails closed on any member key outside the digested and annotation partitions. Recomputed on every CI run by scripts/check_afp_interface_surface.py.

document_axis.note: The current editorial axis. It identifies the published specification document, must match the front-matter `**Document revision:**` line, and moves independently of the interface version and interface digest. Nothing in protocol-family/interface-manifest-v1.json references it; the checker rejects any such family pin.

version_discipline.interface_change: Adding, retiring or renaming a message class, telemetry predicate, typed wire record identifier, presentation profile, or published profile; changing the session envelope identifier or the NATS subject root; changing a predicate's frozen status or its public-input structure identifier; adding, removing, renaming, reordering or retyping a field of any typed `afp:*` wire record or public-input structure; changing a field's canonical encoding or its projection into a composed protocol's fixed-width input; or moving a composed-with version (ZKA, ZKC, or AFP-KDC). The identifier/composition group moves interface_set_id; field-level encoding and projection changes do not (see digest_scope) and require their explicit byte/value conformance pins instead.
rules: Every interface change MUST move interface_version, except the single exhausted dependency-baseline exception enumerated in the next rule. An identifier-granular or composed-version change MUST also move interface_set_id. A change limited to record or public-input fields is detected by the byte-identical FROZEN_* pins and does not move the identifier-granular digest. last_breaking_interface_version identifies the current minimum AFP interface version that a family pin must cover.

Exhausted dependency-baseline exception: document revision 13 at epoch zka:protocol-family:2026-09-03.3 moves the composed ZKA target from 0.9.0-draft to 0.9.1-draft and moves interface_set_id while retaining AFP 0.3.10-draft, because the already-published canonical epoch pins that AFP version and an AFP version change would require another coordinated canonical epoch. This exception applies only to that exact transition and publication; it MUST NOT be reused for any later composed-version change.

A document-only change MUST move document_revision and the specification's `**Document revision:**` line, and MUST leave interface_version and interface_set_id unchanged without requiring a protocol-family action.

Correcting a reference implementation that emitted a value excluded by an already-published typed record does not change that record's interface when its identifier, field set, field order and field types remain byte-identical. The correction MUST reject the non-conforming value, document the rolling-upgrade consequence, and require a fresh message rather than silently translating unauthenticated data. Clarifying previously unspecified signature coverage over those same frozen fields follows the document axis; changing a previously specified signature preimage is an interface change.

The family manifest MUST pin AFP by at least the interface version. A pin on the specification's `**Version:**` header is accepted while it is the published form, but a json_pointer_equals on /interface_version plus /interface_set_id of this file is the intended form: it discriminates the surface rather than a line of prose.

The family manifest MUST NOT pin this file by whole-file sha256, in artifact_bindings or as a projection assertion. A file digest moves on prose edits and trains reviewers to re-bless a digest that moved for non-protocol reasons; interface_set_id excludes prose from its preimage by construction and does not.

The family manifest MUST NOT pin docs/afp_specification.md by whole-file sha256 either, in artifact_bindings or as a projection assertion. That document carries the document-revision axis, so a file digest on it re-couples every editorial edit to a family epoch action even while this file's own gate stays green -- the same defect one file over. text_contains assertions on stable normative strings in the specification remain acceptable; a whole-file digest does not. scripts/check_afp_interface_surface.py rejects both shapes on both paths.

interface_set_id is IDENTIFIER-granular and does not commit to the field content of the typed records (see digest_scope). A change to a record's fields is still an interface change under this section and still MUST move interface_version; it is detected by the byte-identical FROZEN_* pins in tests/python/, not by interface_set_id. A green interface_set_id is not evidence that no record gained a field.

The family manifest MUST NOT reference document_revision, the `**Document revision:**` line, or any document-revision label. Re-coupling the editorial axis to the family manifest reintroduces exactly the friction this file removes.

A family pin naming an interface version AFP has not published, or lagging last_breaking_interface_version, fails AFP's own gate: a breaking AFP interface change cannot be silently combined with an epoch pinned to an older surface.

interface_version_label.note: The family discriminates AFP 0.3.14-draft by text_contains on the specification header while independently pinning the identifier-granular interface_set_id below.

interface_digest.note: The canonical family pins /interface_set_id directly. It never pins this file or the specification by whole-file digest.

consumer_gate.description: The checks AFP's own CI executes on every pull request, and that a downstream consumer's CI SHOULD execute against an AFP checkout before relying on AFP's interface surface.
